items.title: Native Stack and C ABI Boundary
Document Resource and Input Buffer Ownership

exceptions.reason: Phase 5 Sections 5.1 through 5.3 implement the binary document boundary, owner-first cleanup, the closed redacted error vocabulary, public documentation, and an export/typespec/protocol scope allowlist; complete the Phase 5 corpus, lifetime, race, and native-baseline integration matrix before activation.

Phases 3 and 4 implement native ownership plus threaded explicit/GC teardown, and Phase 5 Sections 5.1 through 5.3 add opaque public reachability, owner-first validation for open and closed state, idempotent deterministic close, and the documented scope lock; retain the exception until the full public lifetime/baseline integration matrix and Phase 6 qualification execute.

Phases 1 through 3 provide build, provenance, C ABI, Zig ownership, lifecycle, sanitizer, and symbol evidence, but the exception remains until later phases add threaded execution, the public API, supported-target qualification, and full Milestone 1 closure evidence before activation.

Phase 4 now implements and integrates retained threaded construction, correlated delivery, cancellation, submission-failure containment, explicit/orphan/GC teardown, application generation cycling, and a preliminary scheduler matrix; Phase 6 must establish the final percentile budget and retain the recorded repeated shared-object unload gap until a supported harness supplies that evidence.

requirements.statement: Milestone 1 shall accept binaries only, and non-binary caller arguments shall raise ArgumentError before native work is submitted.
SimdJson.close/1 shall return :ok only after the owner's exactly-once native cleanup has completed and shall return a structured not_owner error when another process supplies a valid document.
SimdJson.close/1 shall raise ArgumentError for values that are not SimdJson.Document resources before native cleanup work is submitted.
Public errors, inspection, logs, and diagnostics shall not include raw JSON, selected source substrings, native addresses, or C++ exception text by default.
The initial stable reasons shall include invalid_json, invalid_utf8, unexpected_eof, out_of_memory, closed, not_owner, and native_failure.
Reported byte offsets shall refer to the logical JSON input and shall never count native padding bytes.
Milestone 1 shall expose no eager decode, projection, streaming, ownership transfer, raw cursor, or raw native-handle API.
SimdJson.Document shall expose an opaque type and a redacted inspection form that reveals no native pointer, input contents, parser state, or generation.
SimdJson.open/1 shall accept one JSON binary and return either {:ok, SimdJson.Document.t()} or {:error, SimdJson.Error.t()}.
SimdJson.Error shall provide a stable reason, optional logical byte offset, optional native diagnostic code, and explanatory message without making message text machine-readable.
SimdJson.open/1 shall admit every valid top-level JSON value, including objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null.
The document resource shall own its padded input, parser, On-Demand document, owner PID, generation, lifecycle state, and lifecycle synchronization for their complete native lifetimes.
Potentially unbounded parser or input teardown shall execute off scheduler rather than inside an ordinary resource destructor callback.
Owner calls to close shall join the shared cleanup operation and return :ok only after the resource is closed and all document-owned native allocations have been released exactly once.
A document shall move monotonically from open to closing to closed, with exactly one winner responsible for native cleanup.
A document shall be represented by an opaque BEAM resource that exposes no native address, parser handle, input pointer, or cursor generation.
Milestone 1 shall copy each accepted input binary into an aligned native allocation with the exact initialized padding required by the pinned simdjson release.
Every future child cursor resource shall retain its parent document resource rather than retain an unowned raw parent pointer.
Cleanup shall prevent new work, invalidate the generation, destroy the On-Demand document, destroy the parser, and release the padded input in dependency-safe order.
Only the process that opened a document shall operate on or close it, and possession of the resource term shall not transfer ownership.
Test builds shall expose bounded native allocation and destruction accounting sufficient to prove baseline recovery without exposing native addresses or input content.
Milestone 1 shall provide no zero-copy input path unless a superseding accepted decision and platform-specific safety evidence authorize it.
A supported target shall build the NIF from a clean checkout without an ambient system simdjson installation or an unverified network fetch during compilation.
Every exported C function shall catch all C++ exceptions and translate them to stable status codes before control returns to Zig.
Native calls shall flow through Elixir, Zigler, Zig, a private C ABI, a C++ shim, and the official simdjson implementation without bypassing the accepted ownership boundary.
The native build shall compile an exact vendored official simdjson release whose tag, commit, source digest, license, and notices are recorded in the repository.
The C ABI shall expose only opaque handles, fixed-width scalar values, validated pointer-length pairs, stable status codes, and matching destruction functions.
Each native layer shall release every allocation it owns when construction fails and shall provide exactly one destruction path for each successful constructor.
The project shall pin every ABI-relevant Zig, Zigler, C++, simdjson, and native build-profile input needed to reproduce a qualified NIF.
Release artifacts shall export only the symbols required by the private C ABI and NIF entry boundary while hiding C++ shim and simdjson implementation symbols.
The repository shall publish and test an explicit supported-target and CPU-dispatch matrix, and unsupported targets shall fail clearly rather than silently using an unqualified build.
Ordinary NIF entrypoints shall perform only bounded validation, resource retention, request correlation, submission, state transition, and bounded result marshalling.
Native work shall check cancellation before parsing, after parsing, before BEAM result construction, and before result delivery while retaining resources across any uninterruptible simdjson call.
Late, duplicate, mismatched, timed-out, cancelled, or caller-orphaned results shall be discarded only after all owned terms, environments, buffers, and resource references are released.
Failure to submit threaded work shall return a structured error and shall never fall back to input-dependent work on a normal or dirty scheduler.
Milestone 1 documentation shall identify threaded execution as a qualification mechanism and shall not claim production admission control before Milestone 4 accepts the bounded worker pool.
Each threaded operation shall use an unforgeable unique reference so only its matching result can complete the waiting Elixir call.
Every queued or running threaded operation shall retain all document and input resources it can dereference until its terminal cleanup completes.

Milestone 1 closure shall require repeatable heartbeat evidence that large concurrent valid and invalid opens and closes preserve a documented normal-scheduler latency budget without using dirty schedulers as the parse queue.

Caller death, application shutdown, and NIF unload shall reject new work, retain in-flight resources to a safe cancellation boundary, suppress orphaned delivery, and release operation-owned state exactly once.
Potentially large native teardown shall follow the accepted off-scheduler policy and shall not execute synchronously on a normal scheduler.
Milestone 1 shall run input-dependent parsing through the pinned Zigler threaded execution facility rather than an ordinary or dirty CPU NIF.
Architecture research shall live under .spec/research, while actionable wrapper milestone documents shall live under docs/milestones and reference the supporting research.
The repository shall define the :simd_json Mix library with a SimdJson root module and an ExUnit test suite.
The Mix project shall pin Zigler as a compile-time-only dependency and shall record compatible BEAM, Zig, C++, simdjson, build-profile, and target inputs in the repository native manifest.
Hex package metadata shall include the exact vendored simdjson source, provenance manifest, patch declaration, and upstream license files required for an offline consumer build.
The Mix project shall include SpecLedEx as a commit-pinned development and test dependency that is excluded from runtime releases.
The repository shall include a .spec/AGENTS.md that tells agents to start a session with mix spec.prime before editing current truth.
The repository shall include a .spec/AGENTS.md that gives local operating guidance for agents working inside the .spec workspace.
The repository shall include a .spec/decisions/README.md that explains when durable ADRs belong in the workspace.
The repository shall include a .spec/README.md that explains purpose, layout, and workflow.
When indexing and validation run, the workspace shall generate .spec/state.json containing indexed subjects, indexed decisions, and verification state.

given: Valid object, array, string, integer, float, true, false, and null documents
then: Each call returns an opaque document
when: Each binary is opened

given: A document owned by process A and shared with process B
then: The non-owner close returns not_owner without changing lifecycle state
Both owner closes return :ok only after native cleanup is complete
when: Process B attempts to close it while it is open
Process A closes it twice

given: A binary, map, reference, and forged SimdJson.Document-shaped value
then: ArgumentError is raised before cleanup work is submitted
No native document lifecycle is changed
when: SimdJson.close/1 is called with each value

given: Empty and whitespace-only binaries
JSON malformed at the beginning, middle, or end
Truncated, invalid UTF-8, and embedded-null JSON binaries
then: Each call returns the appropriate stable reason
Any available byte offset is relative to the logical input
No partially usable document is returned
when: Each input is opened

given: The completed Milestone 1 public modules and documentation
then: Only the document open, close, type, and structured error surface is present
Decode, projection, streaming, cursor, transfer, and native-handle operations are absent
when: Their exported functions and types are enumerated

given: An iolist, atom, map, or other non-binary argument
then: ArgumentError is raised before native work is submitted
when: SimdJson.open/1 is called

given: A valid JSON object binary
then: Open returns an opaque SimdJson.Document
Inspection reveals no native or input details
Close returns :ok
when: Its owner opens and closes the document

given: Malformed JSON containing a unique sensitive marker and an injected native exception message
then: The sensitive input marker is absent
The native address and raw C++ exception text are absent
Stable reason and safe location metadata remain available
when: The error is returned, inspected, and logged through default diagnostics

given: An open document whose owner does not call close
then: Cleanup is admitted exactly once through the off-scheduler path
A normal scheduler does not synchronously perform unbounded teardown
when: The resource becomes unreachable and garbage collection runs

given: A valid JSON binary used to open a document
then: The open native document remains valid
The parser reads only the logical input and initialized padding owned by the resource
when: Every BEAM reference to the original input is dropped and garbage collection runs

given: A recorded native allocation baseline
Batches of documents released by explicit close and by garbage collection
then: Document, parser, buffer, operation, and retained-resource counts return to baseline
Native leak and double-destruction checks remain clean
when: Every explicit close has returned and all admitted garbage-collection cleanup has completed

given: A document opened by process A and its Elixir term sent to process B
then: The call returns a structured not_owner error
The document lifecycle and generation do not change
when: Process B attempts a document operation or close

given: Failure injected after each allocation step during open
then: Every completed allocation is released in dependency-safe order
No usable document resource is returned
when: Document construction aborts

given: One successfully opened document
then: Every close call returns :ok
The On-Demand document, parser, and input buffer are each released exactly once before close returns
Native sanitizer checks report no double free or use-after-free
when: Its owner calls close repeatedly and the BEAM later destroys the resource

given: An independent native harness linked only to the public C header and private C ABI artifact
then: Success and failure use only documented opaque handles and stable status values
Invalid inputs do not crash or expose a C++ exception
Every successful or partial allocation is released exactly once
when: It opens valid object, array, and scalar inputs
It submits malformed, empty, null-pointer, invalid-length, and injected allocation-failure cases
It destroys successful and null handles repeatedly through the documented contract

given: A clean checkout on a target listed as supported
The pinned Elixir, Zig, Zigler, C++, and simdjson inputs
then: The NIF is produced from the recorded vendored source
The selected simdjson runtime implementation is reported by qualification diagnostics
Repeating the build uses the same recorded inputs
when: The release native build runs without a system simdjson package

given: A native test seam that injects a known C++ exception and an unknown C++ exception
then: No exception crosses the C ABI
Each failure becomes its documented numeric status
Every partially created allocation is released exactly once
when: Each failure crosses the C++ shim boundary

given: A proposed simdjson or ABI-relevant toolchain upgrade
then: Provenance, license, clean-build, ABI conformance, sanitizer, and scheduler evidence are regenerated before acceptance
when: Its source or version pin changes

given: A release-mode NIF and native shim for a supported target
then: Only the required NIF entry and private C ABI symbols are visible
No C++ standard-library, shim-internal, or simdjson implementation symbol is exported
when: Their dynamic symbol tables are inspected

given: A target absent from the qualified support matrix
then: The build fails with an explicit unsupported-target diagnostic
No fallback system library or unqualified parser implementation is used
when: The native build is attempted

given: A threaded document open whose caller is alive at admission
then: Native input and operation resources remain valid until the next safe cancellation boundary
No result is delivered to another request
All operation-owned state is eventually released exactly once
when: The caller exits while simdjson is running

given: Multiple large unreachable documents
then: Unbounded teardown is transferred to off-scheduler cleanup
Normal scheduler heartbeats remain within the qualification budget
when: Garbage collection triggers their resource callbacks

given: Independent BEAM heartbeat processes with a documented latency budget
Concurrent large valid and invalid JSON inputs
then: Heartbeats continue within the qualification budget
Normal NIF entry latency remains bounded
Dirty scheduler utilization does not show JSON parsing as the general work queue
when: Documents are repeatedly opened and closed

given: A test environment that supports repeated NIF load and unload
Queued, running, completed, and abandoned native operations
then: New work is rejected once shutdown starts
No completion is delivered through an unloaded or stale native generation
Every retained resource and operation allocation is eventually released exactly once
when: The application and NIF are repeatedly stopped, unloaded, and loaded

given: Two concurrent callers with distinct request references
then: Each caller accepts only its own result
The forged or stale result cannot complete either call
Discarded result state is cleaned safely
when: Results arrive in the opposite order and a forged or stale reference is injected through a test seam

given: A test seam that rejects threaded work submission
then: The call returns a structured native_failure error
Parsing does not run on a normal or dirty scheduler
Retained arguments and partial resources are released
when: A caller opens a document

meta.summary: Milestone 1 exposes binary open and idempotent close through opaque documents and stable structured errors.
Documents own padded input, parser state, lifecycle metadata, and single-process authority through one opaque BEAM resource.
Milestone 1 builds a reproducible native stack around an opaque, exception-safe C ABI.
Input-dependent parse and cleanup work execute through a correlated Zigler-threaded boundary outside normal and dirty schedulers.
Elixir library scaffold, pinned native build tooling, local specification tooling, and implementation roadmap.
Canonical workspace contract for authored specs and generated Spec Led state.
